title: “The largest empire in history” is a statement about maps
cover:
The largest empire?
Depends on the map.

scenes.text: “The largest empire in history.” That phrase is not about governments. It is about maps.
The numbers behind the rankings come from historical atlases: they measure the coloured patch the atlas paints for each empire.
That way, the British Empire reaches about 35 million square kilometres around 1920. The Spanish, 13 to 14 million around 1780.
But painting a territory is not governing it. One colour can hide colonies, protectorates and mere claims.
And the alternative effective control figures going around? They don't hold up either: they don't say which year they measure, or by what rules.
The useful question is not which one was bigger, but what each one really controlled, where and when.
Share it before your next argument about empires.
